title: Nashville's DJ Neha Turns Diwali Into a Dance Floor for a Growing Community
excerpt: With roughly 25,000 people of Indian descent in the Nashville area, DJ Neha's Diwali parties have become a fixture of Music City's festival season — a place where generations and backgrounds meet on the dance floor.
body:
• Roughly 25,000 people of Indian descent live in Nashville and surrounding areas including Franklin and Mt. Juliet, according to US Census Bureau estimates compiled by Neilsberg Research.
  • DJ Neha, a Nashville-based fusion specialist who started a decade ago, has become the region's leading DJ for Indian weddings and a fixture of Diwali season.
  • Her latest Diwali party, on October 23 at Love and Exile Bar, drew revellers dancing in the festival ahead of the main Diwali day on November 8, 2026.
  • For Nashville families, Diwali events this year cluster around the weekends of November 7-8 and November 14-15, with temple celebrations and association gatherings across the metro.

Music City is pulsing with the beat of backyard bhangra. In Nashville, Diwali now has a resident DJ.

The Nashville-based global music fusion specialist who goes by DJ Neha started her career a decade ago and quickly found her niche as the region's leading DJ for Indian weddings, according to The Tennessean. She performs at a wide variety of events across Music City, including shows for the Predators, and travels routinely for gigs — but her parties have become the go-to destination for anyone celebrating Diwali in Tennessee.

"Diwali celebrates good over evil, light over darkness, and knowledge over ignorance. To me, Diwali is about light, hope, gratitude, and new beginnings."

— DJ Neha, Nashville DJ

A community that has reached critical mass

The audience exists because the community does. According to US Census Bureau estimates compiled by Neilsberg Research, there are roughly 25,000 people of Indian descent living in Nashville and the surrounding areas, including Franklin and Mt. Juliet — enough to sustain temple celebrations, association galas and, now, a commercial Diwali party scene.

"It's been beautiful seeing Nashville grow into a diverse community," Neha said. "In Nashville, the energy is super different. The expectations for music are very high, especially for pop and country and fusion beats. Guests come from all around the world." Revellers joined her latest party on October 23 at Love and Exile Bar, dancing to welcome in the festival.

The dance floor as the point

For Neha, the mixing is the message. "As a DJ, one of my favourite things is watching people from different backgrounds and different generations come together on a dance floor," she told The Tennessean. "To me, that captures the spirit of Diwali beautifully — sharing joy, celebrating our roots, and bringing light into each other's lives."

What Nashville families can plan around

Diwali's main day falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, so community events cluster around the weekends of November 7-8 and November 14-15, when temples host Lakshmi Puja and Annakut and associations stage their biggest gatherings, according to NashDesi's Nashville Diwali guide. The five-day festival runs from Dhanteras on November 6 to Bhai Dooj on November 10 — with DJ nights like Neha's now a standard part of how the city marks it.
